source_grounding.call_chain_traced: Full deterministic chain for a standalone (cluster-disabled) deployment, which is the tested sandbox (container testvdb-qdrant-standalone, image qdrant/qdrant:v1.18.0; clone HEAD db3fca3 == server self-reported commit db3fca327851e360c521065649e0f65a57fe7d3c per deployment_meta.json): (1) main.rs init_channel_service leaves id_to_address empty when !is_distributed_deployment; (2) cluster_api.rs get_cluster_telemetry derives all_peers from id_to_address keys -> empty -> FuturesUnordered empty -> telemetries=[]; (3) distributed_telemetry.rs resolve_telemetries: newest_telemetry(&[]) returns None -> StorageError::service_error("Could not get telemetry from cluster") (the exact body string observed); (4) actix/helpers.rs:247 maps ServiceError -> HTTP 500. Query-param validation is present and functional (ClusterTelemetryParams range(min=1) -> the 422/400 responses in sibling logs), so the 500 is NOT an input-handling artifact - it is the missing local/standalone telemetry-collection path: the code treats 'zero telemetries collected' as an unconditional service error instead of degrading to local telemetry or a mode-appropriate response. No by-design comment marks this 500 as intended (the main.rs doc-comment documents the empty-map mechanism, not an intent for the endpoint to fail; the nearest maintainer annotation is the TODO at cluster_api.rs L23-25 acknowledging incomplete handling in this very endpoint).
source_grounding.outcome_note: validation_absent means: the source contains no handling required to satisfy the documented 200 disposition on a default (standalone) deployment - no local-telemetry fallback, no mode-appropriate 4xx, no guarded early return; the unguarded empty-set -> service_error path at distributed_telemetry.rs:158 is the precise gap. by_design_in_source was considered and rejected: no explicit intent evidence (no 'intentionally'/'by design'/'we don't guarantee' comment covers this behavior). Clone is a single-commit checkout (git log shows only db3fca3 'tq renormalization for l2 (#8989)'), so no blame history was available for intent archaeology.

request_typo: params=None is the documented no-param form; the second leg used the documented details_level=0 form; URL taken verbatim from raw_knowledge, not hand-built
mundane_explanation.surviving: deployment-mode dependence: the 500 is only reachable when the cluster is disabled (standalone default); with a cluster-enabled deployment id_to_address is non-empty and the endpoint returns 200 (the doc example itself shows number_of_peers:1). The documentation places no cluster-enabled restriction on the endpoint and documents no error disposition for it, while the same family's GET /cluster degrades gracefully (200, result.status:'disabled') in the identical mode. Whether 'documented 200 unmet on the default standalone deployment' is adjudicated as a product defect or an implicit distributed-only contract is left to the chain-auditor; the evidence here establishes the behavior is deterministic, mode-triggered, and unannotated in both doc and source.
